    Finite representable projective presentations #

    Every finite-support finite-dimensional covariant linear module is generated by finitely many elements. Linear coyoneda turns those generators into an epimorphism from a finite sum of representables, and the same construction on its kernel gives an exact two-step projective presentation. Fullness of linear coyoneda records the first differential as a literal finite matrix of representing-object morphisms, matching the Nakayama push-down interface.

    IsEssentialEpi f ↔ QuotientSubmoduleEquidistribution.IsRightMinimal f

    For finite modules, essential projective epimorphisms and right-minimal projective epimorphisms are equivalent without an extra Hopfian hypothesis.
